extracted.intended_audience: Guardian News & Media journalists, casual workers, freelancers and external contributors
extracted.subtask_description: Organisational editorial code and guidance setting the ethical, legal and professional standards for Guardian and Observer journalism worldwide, covering accuracy, privacy, sourcing, children, images, public interest and staff conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists must take care not to publish inaccurate, misleading or distorted information or images, including headlines not supported by the text. Significant inaccuracies, misleading statements or distortions must be corrected promptly and with due prominence, and — where appropriate — an apology published. A fair opportunity to reply should be given when reasonably called for. Distinguish clearly between comment, conjecture and fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant corrections should be handled through the readers' editor. Headlines must be supported by copy. Distinguish editorialising from factual reporting. See editorial code guidance A on accuracy and objectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Everyone is entitled to respect for private and family life, home, health and correspondence, including digital communications. Editors must justify intrusions into private life without consent. It is unacceptable to photograph individuals without consent in places where there is a reasonable expectation of privacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for complainant's public disclosures and whether material is already public. Obtain senior duty editor authorisation before intrusive reporting. Follow Omand principles (see R). Consult editorial legal where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harassment
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists must not engage in intimidation, harassment or persistent pursuit. They must not persist in questioning, telephoning, pursuing or photographing individuals once asked to desist; must not remain on property when asked to leave; and must identify themselves as a GNM journalist if requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors must ensure compliance by their teams and avoid using non-compliant material from other sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intrusion into grief or shock
rubrics_metrics.description: In cases involving personal grief or shock, inquiries and approaches must be made with sympathy and discretion, and publication handled sensitively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should not restrict reporting of court proceedings. Wait until death is formally confirmed and family notified in most cases; exceptions if public interest or practicability require earlier reporting. Avoid approaches that may harass grieving people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting suicide and self-harm (code)
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting suicide or self-harm, journalists should be conscious of the risk of encouraging others and therefore avoid excessive detail of the methods used, while taking into account the media’s right to report legal proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid excessive method detail; see guidance W for more detailed rules including avoiding triggering images and appending helpline information when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children (general protections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Children (anyone aged 17 or under) should not be approached or photographed at school without permission; must not be interviewed or photographed on welfare issues without parental/guardian consent; must not be paid for material about themselves unless clearly in their interest; and editors must not use a parent's fame as sole justification for publishing details of a child’s private life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors must consult senior duty editor and legal for exceptions. Consider online longevity and withholding identities to protect children as they grow older.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children in sexual offence cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists must not identify children aged 17 or under who are victims or witnesses in sexual offence cases, even if legally free to do so. In reports the child must not be identified; adults may be identified subject to court orders; the word 'incest' must not be used where it could identify a child; ensure nothing implies the relationship between accused and child.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires high caution; consult senior duty editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospitals
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists must identify themselves and obtain permission from a responsible executive before entering non-public areas of hospitals or similar institutions. Restrictions on intruding into privacy are particularly relevant for inquiries about individuals in hospitals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek permission from hospital executives before entering non-public areas; consult clause 8 guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of crime
rubrics_metrics.description: Relatives or friends of accused/convicted persons should not generally be identified without consent unless genuinely relevant. Pay particular regard to naming victims, graphic/invasive details, and images that compromise dignity. Avoid naming children arrested prior to youth court unless already public or with parental consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This should not restrict reporting of legal proceedings; exercise sensitivity for victims and witnesses; consult legal for complex cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clandestine devices and subterfuge (code)
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists must not obtain or publish material acquired using hidden cameras, clandestine listening devices, intercepting private communications, unauthorised removal of documents or by accessing digitally held information without consent. Misrepresentation or subterfuge is only justifiable in the public interest and when material cannot be obtained by other means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any such action requires clear public interest justification and senior duty editor approval; consult editorial legal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Victims of sexual assault
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists must not identify victims of sexual assault or publish material likely to lead to identification unless there is adequate justification and they are legally free to do so; permission from relevant senior duty editor is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High threshold for identification; consult senior duty editor and legal services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discrimination and incitement to hatred
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists must avoid prejudicial or pejorative reference to protected characteristics (race, colour, ethnicity, nationality, religion, age, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, physical or mental illness). Details of such characteristics must be avoided unless genuinely relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow style guide and specific guidance on language for protected characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists must not use for personal profit financial information received in advance of general publication, nor pass such information to others. Must disclose and avoid writing about shares where they or close family have significant financial interest without disclosure, and must not trade on topics they have written about.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose interests to editor/head of business. Do not buy/sell shares about which you have recently written or plan to write.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists have a moral obligation to protect confidential sources of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use secure methods (SecureDrop), attend training provided by editorial legal and InfoSec, and comply with encryption standards. Consult editorial legal and InfoSec as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Witness payments in criminal trials
rubrics_metrics.description: No payment or offer of payment to a witness (or person who may be called as witness) should be made once proceedings are active; prohibition lasts until suspect freed unconditionally or proceedings discontinued or verdict announced. Where proceedings are not active but foreseeable, payments must not be made; rare exceptions require senior duty editor and legal approval. Any payment made to someone later cited as witness must be disclosed to prosecution and defence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Never make payments conditional on trial outcome. Discuss rare exceptions in advance with senior duty editor and editorial legal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment to criminals
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment or offers for stories/pictures/information that seek to exploit or glamorise crime must not be made to convicted/confessed criminals or their associates. Payment invoking public interest requires demonstrating public interest; if no public interest emerges material should not be published. Any payment must be discussed in advance with senior duty editor and director of editorial legal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High bar for payments; consult senior editors and legal; avoid payments that glorify crime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and invocation of the public interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Public interest may include detecting/exposing crime or serious impropriety; protecting public health/safety; protecting public from being misled; disclosing failures to comply with obligations; disclosing miscarriage of justice; raising matters of public debate; disclosing concealment. Freedom of expression itself is a public interest consideration. Consideration of whether material is already public and contribution to debate matters. Exceptional public interest needed to override protections for children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss invoking public interest with senior editors and editorial legal at the outset. Journalists must be able to demonstrate reasonable belief that publication was proportionate and served the public interest and explain the decision at the time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and objectivity (guidance A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should strive to be accurate, fair and objective; significant errors corrected promptly; journalists should recognise how personal biases could affect reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send significant corrections through the readers' editor. News journalists should actively counteract bias and seek fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymous contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles should only be published anonymously/pseudonymously in exceptional circumstances (e.g., safety, privacy, livelihood risks). Permission of relevant senior duty editor is required. Regular anonymous columns require editor-in-chief or equivalent approval. Readers should be made aware when identities are obscured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider motive and alternatives; established pseudonyms are exempt; coordinate with readers' editor and legal if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymous quotations
rubrics_metrics.description: Anonymous quotations should generally be avoided. Use only when necessary to give readers a truer understanding; anonymous pejorative quotes only in rare circumstances after consultation with senior duty editor. Paraphrase anonymous pejorative quotes unless specific approval obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware anonymous quotes confer an unfair advantage on unchallengeable speakers and reduce source assessment. Discuss with senior duty editor; consider confidential sources rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children (guidance D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Special care with children; anyone 17 or under treated as a child. Significant intrusions into children's private lives require strong public interest justification; consider withholding identities because of online longevity; do not photograph or interview without parental responsibility consent on welfare matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss exceptional cases with senior duty editor and editorial legal. Applies when children are subjects or authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital enhancement of images and multimedia
rubrics_metrics.description: Video, audio, images, montages and illustrations should generally not be digitally enhanced or altered. Rare exceptions must be approved in advance by senior duty editor and clearly labelled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label any alterations clearly. See also P (pictures) for further guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct quotations
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct quotations should not be changed to alter their context or meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the Guardian's style guide for quote-handling; do not alter quotes in ways that change meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Errors and amendment requests (guidance G)
rubrics_metrics.description: GNM's policy is to correct significant errors as soon as possible. Complaints, corrections and requests for amendment/deletion should be brought to the readers' editor. Journalists must cooperate frankly and openly and in a timely fashion with the readers’ editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read daily correction columns; follow readers' editor procedures for corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generative AI
rubrics_metrics.description: Generative AI includes systems that create text, images, video, audio or code. Material created using generative AI raises issues around bias, ownership, plagiarism and unreliability. AI should not be used to generate text or images intended to be directly inserted into published journalism except in exceptional circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any exceptional AI use requires explicit senior duty editor approval and must be clearly signalled to readers on the article itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grief (guidance I)
rubrics_metrics.description: People should be treated with sensitivity during periods of personal grief and trauma. Avoid exacerbating distress through intrusive or insensitive reporting and unnecessary/sensational details. Wait for formal confirmation of death and notification of family where practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider international readership; avoid harassment; respect requests to desist. Consult senior duty editor for difficult situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance labels and distressing content
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphic or violent descriptions/depictions should be included only when essential. Where audio/video/photos are editorially justified but distressing, consider prefacing with warnings, explanations or labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labels are not generally necessary on articles where headline/trails indicate subject matter. Use warnings sparingly and appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviewees
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat interviewees with respect, fairness and dignity; ensure they understand they are speaking to a journalist with a view to publication. Off-the-record/background-only conversations must have clear terms. Take special care with victims, children and vulnerable people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give interviewees chance to understand questions and context. Consult senior duty editor for off-the-record agreements or for interviews involving vulnerable subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of language reflects values; adhere to Guardian and Observer style guide. Take care on sensitive issues including protected characteristics, suicide and self-harm. Almost never use swearwords outside direct quotes; avoid them in headlines and standfirsts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add footnotes to support organisations when appropriate. Avoid casual usage of offensive words; consult style guide sections on swearwords and racial terminology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major incident reporting and unfolding events
rubrics_metrics.description: Remain objective, verify before publication, avoid speculation, stereotypes and sensationalist language when reporting major incidents. Talk to senior duty editor before publishing or linking to live footage or material by perpetrators. Consider safety of individuals caught up in events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant clauses include accuracy, privacy, harassment, grief, children and hospitals. Consult Ipso guidance and RUSI report as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mental health
rubrics_metrics.description: Take particular care with mental health stories; do not mention/speculate about a person's mental health unless directly relevant. Include helpline information where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to style guide section on mental health. Provide appropriate helplines by jurisdiction when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open court reporting and inquests
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting from open court/inquests is generally safe legally if fair and accurate, but careful consideration should be given to publishing invasive, insensitive or graphic details or images that could compromise dignity or privacy even if given in open court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify inclusion of graphic details; consult senior duty editor before publishing particularly graphic material. See legal guidance on contempt of court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pictures and video
rubrics_metrics.description: Take care when using images/footage that may be invasive, insensitive or graphic. Consider human dignity when selecting images and avoid disrespectful imagery for sensitive issues. Government handout photos should be used only if they have news value and labelled as such.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult picture desk if in doubt. Coordinate with privacy, harassment, children, digital enhancement and guidance labels policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists must not represent others’ work as their own. Do not reproduce other people’s material without attribution except in exceptional circumstances and only with senior duty editor approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribution is mandatory; seek permission when source cannot be identified or when republishing others' material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy guidance: photography & identifying details
rubrics_metrics.description: Care when taking photos/filming where individuals have reasonable expectation of privacy or are unaware their image will be published; caution about publishing identifying details like street names and house numbers that may endanger privacy or safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-lens use not prohibited but can be a factor in judging intrusion. Follow Omand questions to justify intrusion. Seek senior duty editor and editorial legal guidance when in doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omand principles (application for privacy intrusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Five questions journalists should ask: 1) Is there sufficient cause? 2) Is there integrity of motive? 3) Are methods proportionate? 4) Is there proper authority? 5) Is there a reasonable prospect of success?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to justify intrusions into privacy; be able to demonstrate public interest justification for both gathering and publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: The right to reply
rubrics_metrics.description: Make every effort to contact people/organisations who are the subject of a story before publication to put allegations to them and give an opportunity to respond; the more serious the allegations, the greater the obligation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider time zones and complexity; consult editorial legal services for best practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a source seeks anonymity/confidentiality, discuss with relevant senior duty editor. Journalists have moral obligation to protect confidential sources and otherwise identify sources as specifically as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow clause 14 and internal source-protection guidance; consult legal and senior editors for complex requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing - social media
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat social media content like any other source; consider legal, copyright and ethical issues before accessing, publishing or sharing material from social media or the internet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarise with GNM social media guidelines and apply the same verification/ethical standards as for traditional sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subterfuge and covert behaviour (guidance V)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify yourself as GNM when gathering material; rare instances of justified subterfuge require prior approval by senior duty editor and editorial legal. Applies to material acquired by others using hidden devices too.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If offered covert material by third parties, immediately seek advice from managing editor and editorial legal. Prior approval is required for any use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suicide and self-harm (guidance W)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise particular care; avoid detailed descriptions of methods, avoid speculation about single motives, avoid trigger images (places, scars), consider relatives' feelings, and usually do not report every detail revealed in inquests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to clause 5; append appropriate helpline notes where appropriate. Use general rather than specific language about substances/methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists must verify information before publication and avoid publishing unverified claims; verification standards apply across reporting including social media-sourced material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use corroboration and authoritative sourcing; be particularly cautious in live/unfolding coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial products and promotions (professional behaviour A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on endorsement and promotion of commercial products; standards to avoid mixing commercial promotion with editorial content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure and separation of commercial/advertising relationships are required; see internal policy for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioning (professional behaviour B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for commissioning work, including transparency about terms and conflicts of interest when commissioning freelance or external contributors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow commissioning rules, freelance charter and approvals required for regular anonymous columns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct at work (professional behaviour C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations for professional behaviour in the workplace, including respectful conduct and not using position for personal advantage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See sections on confidentiality, outside interests and social media conduct for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality (professional behaviour D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff must maintain confidentiality around internal processes, sources and sensitive information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow internal protocols on information security and editorial confidentiality; consult managing editor when unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy approval (professional behaviour E)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules about who may approve copy and the process for editorial sign-off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow newsroom hierarchies and approval processes; senior editors have authorising roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credits (professional behaviour F)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on crediting contributors, photographers and other creators appropriately in published content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure correct attribution and credit lines; follow policies for images/third-party material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declarations of corporate interest (professional behaviour G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff must declare corporate/organisational interests that could create conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare such interests on biographies and to managing editor; consult when unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declarations of personal interest (professional behaviour H)
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff must declare personal interests (financial, relationships, roles) that could compromise editorial integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare on staff biographies and consult managing editor about potential conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial reporting (professional behaviour I)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for reporting on financial matters to avoid conflicts and insider trading-like behaviours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose interests and avoid trading on privileged information; coordinate with business editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freebies (professional behaviour J)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gifts and offers of free travel/accommodation must be handled with strict rules: low-value gifts (< £50) should be returned/donated; travel/accommodation borne by third parties must be disclosed and approved; staff should generally not be accompanied on free trips.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose sponsored travel in footnotes; acceptance conditional on editorial freedom; pay additional costs for companions; consult managing editor for exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freelance work and media appearances (professional behaviour K)
rubrics_metrics.description: Full-time staff should not contribute to other publications or media outlets without prior authorisation. Staff should coordinate media appearances via the communications team and seek approval for filming inside GNM offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact media.enquiries@theguardian.com for appearances; prior approval required for outside contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: GNM connections (professional behaviour L)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use GNM position to seek personal benefit, discounts, or quicker service; do not use GNM email/accounts for non-GNM matters or cite Guardian connection to resolve consumer grievances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain separation between personal/business activities and GNM role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offers of financial assistance (professional behaviour M)
rubrics_metrics.description: GNM and journalists should not act as intermediaries for donations; staff should not set up crowdfunders connected to Guardian articles or link to fundraising appeals without senior duty editor approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put parties in contact if both agree but do not act as intermediaries; approval needed for linking to fundraising appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outside interests and engagements (professional behaviour N)
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists have private lives but outside interests must not conflict with GNM duties. Active political involvement may create perceived conflicts; generally not appropriate for staff to hold political office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss intended outside activities (political roles, outside employment, giving evidence, public speaking) with editor-in-chief or managing editor; disclose interests on biographies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payments for stories (professional behaviour O)
rubrics_metrics.description: GNM does not pay sources or interviewees for stories; rare exceptions must be approved by senior duty editor. Journalists should not engage paid non-journalistic agents without approval; tip fees to bona fide freelance journalists may be paid on occasion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult senior duty editor and follow witness payment rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationships (professional behaviour P)
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should not commission, write about, photograph or make editorial decisions about individuals with whom they have a close personal or financial relationship. Consider whether relationships with public figures or other journalists create conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss potential conflicts with managing editor and consider recusal or transparent disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media conduct (professional behaviour Q)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat people with respect and professionalism on social media; remember private posts can be shared publicly; follow GNM social media guidelines and safety guidance on responding to abuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarise with internal social media and online safety documents on the intranet 'Spike'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source care and protection (professional behaviour R)
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should understand limitations of source protection methods, not promise outcomes outside GNM control, attend training on source protection, consult InfoSec, and use secure contact methods (e.g., SecureDrop).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep electronic devices up to date and compliant with InfoSec encryption standards; use secure communication methods and attend training by editorial legal and InfoSec.
